topic: How can beamforming and transponder allocation adapt to dynamic Doppler shifts in LEO mega-constellations for SC-FDMA uplinks?
response: To adapt to dynamic Doppler shifts in LEO mega-constellations for SC-FDMA uplinks, beamforming and transponder allocation can be dynamically adjusted based on the estimated Doppler shift. This can be achieved through real-time monitoring of user terminal velocities and satellite positions. The frequency bandwidths for feeder links (BW_i_FD) and user links (BW_i_UD) can also be adjusted accordingly to minimize frequency synchronisation errors.
reference_context: The context provides information on the impact of Doppler shifts in LEO satellite communications, with a maximum Doppler shift of approximately 9.3 kHz at a carrier frequency of 20 GHz for a 500 km/h relative user mobility.
